nodes.text: Let $h(n)$ be such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line and no four on a circle, determine at least $h(n)$ distinct distances. Does $h(n)/n\to \infty$?

#98 : [Er75f,p.101] [Er83c] [Er87b,p.167] [Er90] [Er92b] [EFPR93] [Er94b] [Er97e] geometry | distances Erdős could not even prove $h(n)\geq n$. Pach has shown $h(n)<n^{\log_23}$. Erdős, Füredi, and Pach [EFPR93] have improved this to\[h(n) < n\exp(c\sqrt{\log n})\]for some constant $c>0$.
